posts.title: Linux Packaging for Taigi Keyboard
posts.description: More easily installable and upgradable packages for siansiansu's Taigi Keyboard . Ubuntu https://launchpad.net/~kisaragi-hiu/+archive/ubuntu/taigikeyboard sudo add-apt-repository ppa:kisaragi-hiu/taigikeyboard sudo apt update sudo apt install fcitx5-taigikeyboard sudo apt install ibus-taigikeyboard Fedora https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/kisaragi-hiu/taigikeyboard/ sudo dnf copr enable kisa

posts.title: let-alist but for any collection
posts.description: let-alist is great: ( let-alist ' (( a . (( b . "nested-value" )))) . a.b ) nested-value but it only supports alists. Surely it's not that hard to make a version that uses (map-elt map key) instead of (cdr (assq key alist)) ? What It sure wasn't. After about 10 minutes of hacking: ( require 'let-alist ) ( defun let-map--list-to-sexp ( list var ) "Turn symbols LIST into recursive calls to `map-elt'

posts.title: Regular expression for checking Taigi words with too many dashes
posts.description: This is in a context with Perl-like regexps (Qt regexps in Lokalize, specifically). I sometimes write Taigi with too many dashes (eg. "kang-khū-lia̍t-hāng-bo̍k" instead of "kang-khū-lia̍t hāng-bo̍k") and wanted to use a regular expression to quickly find instances of this. With English we can just to (\w+)-(\w+)-… to find sequences of word characters. \w doesn't match accented characters though. U
